factions.name: Richmond Consilium
factions.public_summary: The city's Awakened mages, organized as a loose Consilium. They hide behind university and hospital cover, and they want a formal claim over investigating the Overwrite before anyone else makes one. The faction is fracturing: junior members feel shut out of the recent closed meetings.

factions.name: Silver Ladder (Richmond)
factions.public_summary: The Richmond reach of the Silver Ladder, the order that believes the Awakened should guide the sleeping world. It works through council seats and procedure, favors order and hierarchy, and holds its position rather than risking it.

factions.name: Canal Court
factions.public_summary: The Kindred who keep the old canal tunnels and quietly own a good share of Downtown through legitimate business fronts. They want stable feeding grounds, which gentrification in the Bottom has disrupted, and a cold standoff with rival Kindred there shows up as territory tension.

factions.name: Hedge Keepers
assets: Artists and creative mortals as watchers
factions.public_summary: The Fan's changelings and their friends, who tend the Doors to the Hedge that open near monuments and venues. The Doors are shifting: some that used to lead somewhere safe now open somewhere wrong, and the Keepers are scrambling to learn why.

factions.name: The Revisionists
assets: Seats in the city planning office
A development easement at the Old Market Site
factions.public_summary: A small, loose Mortalis circle working through the city planning office and local historical societies. Few people outside it could name a member. It recently filed an easement that delays development at the Old Market Site for eighteen months, with no reason given.

factions.name: The Morrow Network
assets: Knowledge of where the Bottom's bodies are buried
factions.public_summary: A family business with supernatural reach, three generations deep in the Bottom. Neutral between Night and Mortalis after decades of doing business with both; pragmatic, and survives by being useful to everyone.

factions.name: East End Tenants
assets: Church-basement supplies and a food pantry
factions.public_summary: The Creighton Court tenant council and its night patrol: a thirty-year organizing network that keeps the community running when official systems fail. Right now it is fighting to stop the Renaissance redevelopment phases from displacing the court.

factions.name: Memorial Keepers
assets: Hollywood Cemetery as claimed neutral ground
Volunteer guides at the War Memorial
Crematory records and a stonemason's eye
factions.public_summary: An uneasy alliance of the bluff's caretakers of the dead, Kindred and mortal alike, who look after the cemetery, the crematory's records, the memorial wall and its lettering. They agree that names must be kept right and disagree on whose version of the past counts, so the alliance is steady but touchy while names on the wall and in the graves keep changing.

factions.name: River Crews
assets: Terminal union hall and shop stewards
Tugs and the river rescue network
Dockside Night money and stamped paperwork
factions.public_summary: The working river's own web: terminal and rail crews, tug hands, the people who stamp the paperwork and the Night money that pays the late shifts. They move cargo by day and quieter goods by night, answer to the tide, and trade favors for a price. Recurring friction comes over who stamps the paperwork.

factions.name: Valley Mutual Aid
assets: Free late-release rides from the courts annex
factions.public_summary: The Valley's own safety net: a church van, a meal line, a free ride service for late releases, a bike stand on the motel lots and off-the-clock interpreting at the courts. Everyone in it has an angle, and the group works to keep people from being moved around any more than they already are. It strains against the annex and holding center, which would prefer people stay unseen.

factions.name: The City Hall Clerks
assets: Chamber transcripts and the clerk's vault
factions.public_summary: The permanent staff of Richmond's government, aides, stenographers and records clerks, together with the go-betweens who work the gap between that staff and everyone else. Informal, practical and gossip-wired, they know where every file lives and who owes whom, and anyone who needs a door opened can buy an introduction, paid in Debt. They want the machinery to keep running, even as the records change between sessions and only the people who keep the originals notice.
